plan.summary: Provisions a compact GKE Autopilot cluster in us-central1 running a containerized Python asyncio stream worker consuming from Cloud Pub/Sub and writing tumbling window aggregates to Firestore Native with Workload Identity Federation.
plan.architecture_overview: The architecture features a GKE Autopilot cluster in us-central1 configured with Workload Identity Federation. A dedicated Kubernetes Service Account (sa-stream-worker) in the stream-apps namespace is mapped to a least-privilege Google IAM Service Account with roles/pubsub.subscriber and roles/datastore.user. Application code is packaged using Cloud Native Buildpacks into Artifact Registry. The deployment provisions 1 replica (cpu: 250m, memory: 512Mi) with an HPA scaling up to 2 pods at 80% CPU utilization, pulling batches from the stream-gke-sub subscription on stream-ingest-topic and persisting 1-minute tumbling window metrics to the stream_metrics Firestore collection.

infra_tasks.title: Enable APIs and Provision Base VPC and Artifact Registry
infra_tasks.description: Enable container.googleapis.com, artifactregistry.googleapis.com, pubsub.googleapis.com, and firestore.googleapis.com. Provision VPC subnet and standard Docker Artifact Registry repository stream-workloads.
acceptance_criteria: All required APIs enabled with disable_on_destroy = false
Artifact Registry Docker repo initialized in us-central1

infra_tasks.title: Provision Pub/Sub Messaging and Firestore Database
infra_tasks.description: Provision Pub/Sub topic stream-ingest-topic, pull subscription stream-gke-sub with max 5 delivery attempts, and Firestore Native database.
acceptance_criteria: Pub/Sub topic and pull subscription created
Firestore Native database initialized

infra_tasks.title: Configure IAM and Workload Identity Federation
infra_tasks.description: Provision dedicated GCP IAM Service Account with roles/pubsub.subscriber and roles/datastore.user, and bind roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser to stream-apps/sa-stream-worker.
acceptance_criteria: GCP Service Account created with least-privilege roles
Workload Identity IAM binding configured

infra_tasks.title: Deploy GKE Autopilot Cluster and Kubernetes Manifests
infra_tasks.description: Provision GKE Autopilot cluster in us-central1 and declare kubernetes_manifest resources: stream-apps Namespace, sa-stream-worker ServiceAccount with Workload Identity annotation, stream-processor-deployment Deployment (cpu: 250m, memory: 512Mi, liveness/readiness probes), and HorizontalPodAutoscaler (target 80% CPU, max 2 replicas).
acceptance_criteria: GKE Autopilot cluster provisioned
Kubernetes manifests applied with correct image and resource limits

code_tasks.title: Develop Asyncio Streaming Worker and Probes
code_tasks.description: Implement Python asyncio worker consuming batches of 50 messages from stream-gke-sub via google-cloud-pubsub async pull, calculating 1-minute tumbling window metrics (throughput, error rate, latency), persisting to Firestore stream_metrics, and exposing HTTP health probe endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Asyncio subscriber processes messages without blocking
Window metrics write to Firestore stream_metrics
HTTP liveness and readiness endpoints return 200 OK

code_tasks.title: Build and Push Container Image to Artifact Registry
code_tasks.description: Package the streaming worker application into a container image using Cloud Native Buildpacks/Cloud Build and push to us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/[PROJECT_ID]/stream-workloads/stream-processor:latest.
acceptance_criteria: Container image successfully compiled and tagged
Image pushed to Artifact Registry repository

code_tasks.title: Implement QA Unit and Integration Test Suite
code_tasks.description: Author pytest suite mocking Pub/Sub pull messages, batch aggregation calculations, Firestore write operations, and health checks with 100% pass rate.
acceptance_criteria: All unit tests pass with mock fixtures
Zero Bandit security issues

plan.risk_assessment: Provisioning a GKE Autopilot cluster takes 10-15 minutes and incurs managed control plane infrastructure. Workload Identity Federation must strictly match Kubernetes namespace and KSA names to prevent authorization failures.
